headline.basis_note: Pre-registered headline: the window (2020-2024) was fixed before the TSA 2025 release was examined (no result-shopping); constant 2019 prices. The value is recomputed from the TSA 2025 revised receipts per the revision policy (later official workbook wins), so it equals the sum of the fragment's own 2020-2024 rows.

supplementary.label: Supplementary only: cumulative real gap 2020-2025 includes the preliminary 2025 year — never quote it as the headline

countries.receipts_basis_note: Tourism Malaysia tourist expenditure survey (Statistics in Brief 2024; consistent with the DOSM TSA inbound consumption aggregate).

MOTS (Ministry of Tourism and Sports) continuous foreign-tourist expenditure survey (departure-point sampling); survey estimates, not balance-of-payments. 2024 headline later restated to ~THB 1.61T by MOTS.
Bank Indonesia tourism foreign exchange (devisa pariwisata), processed by Kemenpar — administrative balance-of-payments, not a visitor survey. No official rupiah figure published.

receipts_2024.usd_note: published in USD (angka sementara); ~Rp265T at ~15,869 IDR/USD is a conversion, not official

excluded_markets.reason: Not comparable: Vietnam publishes only TOTAL tourism revenue (international + domestic, ~840T VND in 2024, an administrative aggregate of provincial estimates). No international-only receipts figure exists, so a defensible 2024 receipts-per-visitor yield cannot be computed; the naive 840T VND / 17.5M arrivals (~US$1,889) overstates the international yield because domestic revenue is in the numerator.

caveats: Basis mix: Malaysia and Thailand receipts are visitor-expenditure SURVEY estimates (Tourism Malaysia; Thailand MOTS departure-point survey); Indonesia's are Bank Indonesia balance-of-payments travel credit (administrative). Cross-country yield gaps of 10-20% can be methodological, not real.

The 2019 baseline for every country is the World Bank WDI receipts-per-visitor (ST.INT.RCPT.CD / arrivals); the current WDI build stops at 2020 for these countries, so 2019 is the latest WDI-comparable yield. The Indonesia 2024-vs-2019 pair is the cleanest (same BI BOP basis); Malaysia's 2024 survey figure vs its 2019 WDI BOP figure is the least clean (survey vs BOP).
Thailand's headline 2024 revenue (THB 1.67T) was later restated to ~THB 1.61T in MOTS's own year-end summary; the headline figure is cited and the restatement flagged.
USD conversions use 2024 average rates (THB ~34.5, MYR ~4.68) or authority-stated conversions where published; per-visitor yields are therefore approximate.
Framing: this regional comparison is supporting context for the Missing Billions (the real-terms 2019-anchor counterfactual), never the headline.

source_segmentation.method: k-means (k=4) on z-scored features, k-means++ init, best of 12 consecutive fixed-seed restarts (seeds 42-53, lowest inertia 53.48 kept); clusters re-labelled by descending mean yield
source_segmentation.naming_rationale: Segment names are derived from cluster profiles by rule, not machine ids: the cluster with the lowest mean yield that also has the highest volume is named 'Volume Traps' (the arrivals KPI over-rewards exactly this short-stay regional traffic - the Volume Trap critique); the cluster with the highest mean yield is named 'High-Yield Long-Haul' (high wallet and development markets, predominantly long-haul, reached by air); among the remaining clusters the one with the strongest arrivals growth is named 'High-Growth Emerging', and any leftover is 'Mid-Yield Steady' or 'Low-Yield Steady' by its mean yield against the panel median. Ties break by the descending-mean-yield cluster order, so names are deterministic.

clusters.naming_rationale: highest mean yield (RM5,371) with lower volume: high-wallet, high-development markets, predominantly long-haul
fastest arrivals growth (+75.6% mean) at a solid mid yield (RM4,591): emerging markets scaling in both volume and value
below-median yield (RM3,406) with flat growth (+4.0% mean): no standout trait yet
lowest mean yield (RM1,675) and highest volume (mean log10 arrivals 6.76): short-stay regional traffic the arrivals KPI over-rewards - the Volume Trap profile
